reasons: narrow: A single nonrefinable control interval can encode values of the miscoverage level arbitrarily close to zero and bounded away from zero simultaneously. For two chi-square degrees of freedom its admissible quantiles then have arbitrarily large spread, so no enclosure can satisfy the frozen relative-width requirement. Exact dyadic controls or polynomial-time refinable dyadic names are the minimal information-model repair; they do not assume the spectral or statistical crux.
REVIEW: assume-the-crux narrowing — a new assume/suppose premise may promote the open obligation into a hypothesis (state the result and leave the construction an open obligation instead)

verdict.note: Accepted both items after independent math consult: refinable names repair a genuine public-input information defect without assuming the numerical/statistical crux, and the implementation theorem proves explicit schedules, containment, and negligible padding rather than assuming them.
